disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with MassWildlife (Division of Fisheries and Wildlife) before hunting or trapping. MGL Ch. 131 §80A: the trap ban exempts municipal boards of health — check city/town rules.

license_summary.hunting_license: Hunting or sporting license required for residents; small game or big game license for non-residents. No additional permit required to hunt bobcat, coyote, or fox.
license_summary.pelt_check: Pelt checking/reporting required for beaver, bobcat, coyote, fisher, fox, mink, and river otter. Bobcats must be reported at an official furbearer check station within 4 working days of harvest (not online); other species within 4 working days of the end of the season for that species.
license_summary.trapping_license: A separate Massachusetts trapping license is required to trap furbearers. Trapper education is mandatory for new trappers.

verification.confirmation_notes: Hunting dates spanning the 2026–27 new year are explicitly published on current MassWildlife regulation pages (bobcat: Dec. 21, 2026 – Mar. 8, 2027; coyote: Oct. 17, 2026 – Mar. 8, 2027; fox: Nov. 2, 2026 – Feb. 27, 2027), all crawled September 2026. Trapping seasons follow fixed annual formulas in 321 CMR 3.02(5), confirmed against MassWildlife's published furbearer trapping table (2025 season summary) — pattern is unchanged year to year. Raccoon/opossum hunting formula (Oct 1 – Jan 31) from 321 CMR 3.02(5)(2). Shotgun deer season Nov 30 – Dec 12, 2026 from the official 2026 Hunting Season Summary.
known_gaps: Scientific names are stated in an official MA source only for bobcat, red fox, and gray fox (321 CMR 3.02(3)(a)); all others are standard taxonomy with scientific_name_verified=false. Weasel is null because regulations do not distinguish weasel species.

No explicit closed-season species list was found in official MA sources (e.g., Canada lynx is excluded from the legal definition of bobcat but no explicit closed-season statement exists); no closed species is modeled for MA.

Pelt check-station mechanics beyond the published 'within 4 working days' rule should be confirmed in the current MassWildlife trapping regulations before field use — noted as reminder-level detail, not legal authority.
Proposed 2026 legislation to allow Sunday hunting had NOT passed as of June 2026 per MassWildlife; if enacted, season dates could shift.
Problem Animal Control (PAC) agent take and beaver emergency-permit take are depredation mechanisms — noted but not modeled as seasons.

Full trap-hardware detail is excluded per schema scope; brief method restriction (box/cage traps or common rat traps; body-grip/leghold/snare restrictions under MGL c.131 §80A) is noted in research notes only.
